title: Tail-supported Hardy control from the R-419 Lyapunov transform
question: Does the positive R-419 tail Lyapunov rate give an exact ground-state-transform identity and a Hardy-type Dirichlet lower bound for functions supported on the tail?

new_perspective.principle: Replace the finite tail drift diagnostic by an exact reversible ground-state transform. The remainder is a manifestly nonnegative weighted square, so a positive tail rate controls tail-supported L2 mass without inventing a pointwise probability floor.
route: Use the R-419 conditional weights pi and symmetric momentum conductance c without changing the Q3 parent, normalization or log-domain convention.
For a positive Lyapunov vector V define LV_i=pi_i^(-1) sum_j c_ij(V_j-V_i) and h_i=-(LV_i)/V_i.
Verify E(f)=sum_i pi_i h_i f_i^2 + (1/2)sum_ij c_ij V_i V_j(f_i/V_i-f_j/V_j)^2 for every finite vector f.
For f zero outside a tail T and h_i>=kappa on T, record E(f)>=kappa sum_{i in T} pi_i f_i^2.
Run the identity on selected R-419 Q3 conditional rows and independently on non-importing reversible graph fixtures; reject sign, support, symmetry and positivity mutations.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: This supplies the exact tail-supported algebra needed by a future Lyapunov/Poincare decomposition. It does not control arbitrary functions with a core offset, establish a global Poincare constant, or provide a common Hamiltonian core or physical gap.

finite_theorem.identity: E(f)=sum_i pi_i h_i f_i^2 + 1/2 sum_ij c_ij V_i V_j(f_i/V_i-f_j/V_j)^2
finite_theorem.tail_consequence: If f vanishes off T and inf_T h_i>=kappa>0, then E(f)>=kappa sum_{i in T} pi_i f_i^2.
finite_theorem.scope_boundary: The tail consequence is not a global Poincare inequality because no control is asserted for a function's core mean or core-to-tail decomposition.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean proves the two-state rational identity, nonnegative remainder and tail consequence; the Q3 matrix rows, arbitrary finite sums, common core and all uniform or physical limits remain executable/open analysis.

assumptions: The R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized, and its projected momentum conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The Lyapunov vector V is strictly positive and the tail is a declared subset on which h_i is bounded below.
The finite Dirichlet form uses the same conductance normalization as R-419.
Tail-supported means f_i=0 for every core index; no global centering is silently assumed.
The Lean cross-check is a two-state algebraic witness, not a formalization of the full Q3 matrix calculation.
missing_assumptions: A volume-, cutoff-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for the R-419 tail rate on one Hamiltonian common core.
A compatible bound for the core mean and core-to-tail boundary term for arbitrary observables.
A uniform induced-core Schur/Poincare estimate and boundary-capacity control.
Two-sided form-norm control of the actual R-399 likelihood histories and a common split-limit map.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
promotion_criteria: Prove the same transform on a declared unbounded Q3 common core with domain and closure control.
Establish uniform tail-rate, core-gap and boundary-capacity bounds under cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion changes.
Add the missing variance decomposition and transfer to the R-399/R-415 history before any GNS or physical promotion.
stop_conditions: A negative tail rate or non-symmetric conductance invalidates the Hardy consequence for that row and requires route repair.
An identity residual beyond tolerance stops promotion and indicates a sign, conductance or normalization defect.
Finite tail-supported control cannot be promoted to global Poincare, a mass gap, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
evidence_level: T0 / exact finite algebra plus executed Q3-row integration; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
non_claims: No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform Hardy constant.
No global Poincare or Schur theorem for arbitrary functions.
No common Hamiltonian core or split-limit dynamics.
No OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise spectral gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.

formal_integration.lean: R421 PASS; two-state algebraic cross-check only

boundary: R-421 closes an exact finite tail-supported identity and its finite Q3 calibration. It does not close the uniform Lyapunov/Poincare, common-core, dynamics, GNS, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A gates.
next_unlock: Prove a domain-controlled version on one Q3 Hamiltonian common core with uniform rate, core/boundary decomposition and R-399 history transfer; only then revisit the global Poincare and broken-sector GNS gates.
no_overclaim: The nonnegative ground-state-transform remainder is an exact algebraic interface, not evidence that the physical tail is controlled in a regulator-independent or thermodynamic limit.
